chapter: Band family, war years and wrap-up
title: Bebop in the band
summary: Bobby Green and Willie Moore played bebop numbers.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Now, you said that the band's style didn't change too much as the group either expanded or fellows were drafted. What about the quality? Did it remain pretty much the same? Or, did you feel the absence of any of the players?

Well, if you're used to listening to the style of another man like, I'll just say an instrument like a tenor solo, and then you got another man with a different style, you felt that for a certain time cause you're used to listening to the other tenor man that helped set that style.
And then that, cause, I had one, Bobby Green, he played real well. He could play bebop good. You know? So, he got in, he played a little, the bebop style. Then,
I put a couple of beebop tunes in my book and (inaudible) arranged it cause beebop was kind of coming in style then cause Dizzy was exploring that. You know?
And then, so when we got the people, like I said, wanted to hear a beebop number, I had it. See, and so he was a good beebop tenor man.
